outcome_intro: Ask your AI to restore or download every CloudAlly mailbox as it stood on a past date, list a mailbox's past backups, or find every customer whose backups are stale or failing. It plans before it acts, records every restore and download in a local ledger, and reads the past backup dates CloudAlly's documented API cannot reach from the customer portal, the same way the partner portal does.

instead_of_say.instead: Opening the CloudAlly restore wizard once per mailbox to put a whole company back to how it was on the 1st, and keeping a spreadsheet of which ones are done
instead_of_say.say: Restore every mailbox on this customer's Microsoft 365 task to its backup from October 1st, and show me the plan first.

instead_of_say.instead: Building a year-end export per mailbox and per sub-source in the portal, then racing 60-second download links one archive at a time
instead_of_say.say: Archive every mailbox as it stood on December 31st in the customer's timezone, and download the archives to disk.

instead_of_say.instead: Clicking into every customer account in the partner portal to look for red backup statuses
instead_of_say.say: Which mailboxes across all my CloudAlly customers have not backed up in two days, or failed?

pain_points: The CloudAlly portal restores and exports one mailbox, one date, one wizard at a time; a company-wide restore or a multi-year legal request is hundreds of trips through the same screens.
The documented CloudAlly API reports only each mailbox's latest backup, so it cannot say which backup existed on a past date.
The documented export call answers 200 and creates no job, and an MS365 mailbox needs a separate download per sub-source with its own timestamp.
Backup timestamps are UTC, so the backup stamped December 31st holds December 30th for a US customer.
Download links expire after 60 seconds, and spotting a failing backup means opening every customer account.

different_vs_wrappers: [cloudally](https://github.com/jancotanis/cloudally) (a Ruby gem) and [n8n-nodes-cloudally](https://github.com/davejlong/n8n-nodes-cloudally) (n8n workflow nodes) wrap CloudAlly's documented API. This one is a single binary that works as a CLI and an MCP server and goes past the documented API where it stops: it reads each mailbox's past backups from the customer portal, creates downloads the way the portal does (the documented export call creates nothing), plans and ledgers bulk restores and downloads to one date, and sweeps every customer's backup health in one command.
different_vs_vendor: The CloudAlly partner and customer portals restore and export one mailbox and one date at a time through a wizard. This works from the AI agent you already use, handles whole tasks and multiple years at once, shows a plan before anything changes, and keeps a local record of every restore and download it started.

faqs.a: Yes, on paid ChatGPT plans. ChatGPT connects to remote MCP servers over HTTPS, and cloudally-mcp speaks HTTP natively: set CLOUDALLY_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN, run `cloudally-mcp --transport http`, and serve its /mcp endpoint (http://127.0.0.1:7777/mcp by default) over HTTPS behind an authenticating proxy that signs ChatGPT in with OAuth and adds the bearer header the server requires. ChatGPT cannot send a fixed bearer token, so a bare tunnel gets HTTP 401. Step-by-step in the install guide.

faqs.q: Do I need to know how to code?
faqs.a: No. Paste one sentence into Claude Code or Codex and your agent does the install, or run a one-line installer. You enter the CloudAlly API client id and secret once and run `cloudally-cli auth login --partner`.

A CloudAlly API application key pair (CLOUDALLY_CLIENT_ID and CLOUDALLY_CLIENT_SECRET, from the partner portal under Integrations > REST API) plus one login: `auth login` for a single company account, or `auth login --partner` for every customer. Past backup dates and downloads need the partner login.

faqs.q: Can it change or delete my customers' backups?
faqs.a: It can, because CloudAlly's API can: restores write back into live mailboxes, and deleting a backup task deletes its data. Every restore and download command shows what it would do and stops until you pass --yes, and governance.md lists the destructive commands an agent should never run on its own. Set CLOUDALLY_MCP_READ_ONLY=1 to give an MCP agent read-only tools.

faqs.q: Why does a December 31st download hold December 30th?
faqs.a: CloudAlly stamps backups in UTC, and a nightly backup runs late in the evening local time, so it is stamped the next UTC day. Pass `download submit --utc-offset -5` (US Eastern, for example) and --on-date then means the customer's own calendar day.

Your data stays on your machine. The CLI, MCP server and local store are all local, the MCP server runs over stdio unless you start it with --transport http, and download links are minted and streamed in one step rather than stored. Credentials are never bundled or transmitted by MSP Skills.
Free. Apache-2.0 licensed. You pay only for whichever AI agent you already use.

governance_summary: This connector can restore into live customer mailboxes, create download jobs and, through CloudAlly's own API, delete backup tasks and their data, so it is not read-only. Every restore and download command prints its plan and stops until --yes is passed, download jobs are only ever EXPORT jobs, and CLOUDALLY_MCP_READ_ONLY=1 limits an MCP agent to reads. The company login (auth login) reaches one customer; the partner login reaches all of them.

safety_tiers.examples: backup health, backup snapshots, restore plan, restore watch, restore history, download list, download watch; every list, get, details, bills, tasks and backup-statuses read; sync, search, export. Local writes only: the response cache, the local store and files you name
download link (a 60-second presigned URL to a mailbox archive) and download fetch (writes complete mailbox archives to disk)
safety_tiers.policy: Human-in-the-loop - never paste a link anywhere

safety_tiers.examples: download submit and download start (EXPORT jobs only); backup-now, activate, pause, add-entity and cancel on backup tasks; creating accounts, resellers and users; updating settings and permissions
restore submit and the recovery restore commands, which write backed-up items back into live mailboxes, sites and drives
safety_tiers.policy: Human-in-the-loop - run restore plan or --dry-run first

safety_tiers.examples: tasks delete and its distributor and reseller variants (delete a backup task and its data; never point one at a download job), remove-entity, unsubscribe and user delete (delete a CloudAlly account), delete-user
auth login, auth use-account, auth set-token, auth logout, session login and refresh, access-token and sign-in-token, user update-password, import
--deliver webhook:<url> on any command, feedback --send, and feedback when CLOUDALLY_FEEDBACK_ENDPOINT is set with CLOUDALLY_FEEDBACK_AUTO_SEND=true
safety_tiers.policy: Human-in-the-loop - a webhook sink moves client data off your machine

safety_tiers.examples: cloudally_execute calls any endpoint of the CloudAlly spec by ID: each call follows the tiers above, and every non-GET call is refused while CLOUDALLY_MCP_READ_ONLY=1

auth_note: Create an API application in the CloudAlly partner portal (Integrations > REST API), set CLOUDALLY_CLIENT_ID and CLOUDALLY_CLIENT_SECRET, set CLOUDALLY_PARTNER_EMAIL and CLOUDALLY_PARTNER_PASSWORD, then run `cloudally-cli auth login --partner` and `cloudally-cli doctor`: it makes one authenticated read to confirm the token works. For a single company, set CLOUDALLY_EMAIL and CLOUDALLY_PASSWORD and run `cloudally-cli auth login` instead.
